cover.album: Shades of Blue: Madlib Invades Blue Note

cards.headline: The keys to the Blue Note vault
cards.snippet: In 2002 Blue Note did something it had never done: it handed a hip-hop producer its master tapes. Madlib — Oxnard's Otis Jackson Jr., a lifelong jazz obsessive — spent the access on Shades of Blue (released 24 June 2003), remixing the catalogue and re-recording parts of it with his own bands. Its longest track, at 7:36, rebuilds Donald Byrd's 'Stepping Into Tomorrow', the title track of Byrd's 1975 jazz-funk album, arranged by Larry Mizell with Stephanie Spruill among its singers. Asked by Blue Note's president Don Was how he picked his two Byrd cuts, Madlib answered: 'I had to get that jazz-funk!'
cards.context: Paste later ranked the album No. 11 on its list of classic hip-hop albums that deserve more attention, and in 2023 Blue Note reissued it in the Classic Vinyl Series, mastered by Kevin Gray.

cards.headline: The villain's denial
cards.snippet: Before the song proper starts, MF DOOM delivers a straight-faced statement over the groove of Bobbi Humphrey's 'Blacks & Blues': he has no prior knowledge of any invasion, and no ties to Madlib. Every layer is a wink. The album is called Madlib Invades Blue Note. The Humphrey sample is the same one DOOM's old group KMD used on 'Plumskinzz', rapped by his late brother Subroc. And the denial was cut while the two were secretly making an album together — Madvillainy, which leaked two months before Shades of Blue was released, so fans in the know heard the joke in real time.
cards.context: Genius annotates the song's title line with this story and credits the track '(Ft. Madvillain)'; Blue Note's own retrospective says DOOM foreshadows the collaboration. Madvillainy was officially released in March 2004.

cards.headline: First, give the credit where it's due
cards.snippet: some comments thinking that this is a madlib original: it's not. madlib went into the blue note catalog and gave select blue note pieces (noteworthy) makeovers. this is donald byrd– check the original to give credit where it's due
cards.context: The thread argues back — one listener calls 'makeovers' a minimizing word for the artistry on display; the author answers that enhancing rather than reworking is exactly what Madlib does.

replies.author: @TheAquaSolution
replies.text: Honestly one of my favorite parts of hip hop. It's exposed me to so much beautiful music I otherwise wouldn't have heard.

replies.author: @dylanrowleyprod
replies.text: I’d say reducing this album to “noteworthy makeovers” really minimizes the artistry Madlib is showing on this project. But that’s just me

cards.headline: 'I have no ties to Madlib'
cards.snippet: “I have no ties to madlib” Madvillain comes out a year later.
cards.context: The intro's denial, quoted back by the thread's favourite joke on the older upload — the album he was denying arrived the following year.

replies.author: @EkosPlatinum
replies.text: He's a villain, word not to be trusted

replies.author: @jeezuschryst
replies.text: I mean, he's also saying that on this MADLIB song...

cards.headline: Dumile, here for no reason
cards.snippet: Ah, Dumile on the intro, and for no reason- telling you that he's here for no reason. That's just pure coolness 😂🙌🔥🔥😂
cards.context: Dumile is DOOM's real name — Daniel Dumile — and the whole performance is him insisting, at length, that he has nothing to do with any of this.

replies.author: @fitforfreelance
replies.text: I heard this album when it came out, this intro hits different after years of their music and his death 😂 so cool

cards.headline: Sixty-five, and hearing it reborn
cards.snippet: I’m 65 years old and this Donald Byrd gem was my jam when I was in college! To hear the rebirth - wow it gives me life! Bravo, young lion!
cards.context: His reply under the top comment completes the circuit: his son sent him Madlib after he had sent his son the Byrd original — each introduced the other.

replies.author: @lee2nice
replies.text: That's just beautiful ❤️ 😍 just played this out tonight at a event, forgot how much I liked it, love original too ✌️ ❤️

cards.headline: Donald Byrd's original (1975)
cards.snippet: The title track of Byrd's album Stepping Into Tomorrow, recorded in December 1974 with Larry Mizell conducting a jazz-funk cast — Gary Bartz, Harvey Mason, Chuck Rainey — with Stephanie Spruill in the backing vocals. One listener: "Thanks To God 50 years later & I’m still stepping Amen"
cards.context: The original's largest thread is full of fifty-year listening histories; its most-liked voice is a friend of Spruill's, testifying that the soprano is hers.

cards.headline: Citrus Sun's faithful cover
cards.snippet: A studio cover of Byrd's title track by Citrus Sun, Jean-Paul "Bluey" Maunick's Incognito side project — Valerie Etienne on vocals, Dominic Glover on trumpet. Uploaded in November 2013; no album release is documented. One listener: "This song will never die!!! Hauntingly beautiful!!"
cards.context: Its small thread spots the Incognito connection before anything else — and one listener wanders in from the Madlib side: "madlib really cooked huh".
